datasets.name: outlook
queryLines:
-- Week-ahead GB power price report: one row for each of the next 7 days.
--
-- Run it daily after the energy_daily job (about 08:30 UK), e.g. as a scheduled Databricks
-- SQL query, a dashboard dataset or an alert. Replace `energy` with your catalog.
--
-- How the estimate works
--   model = a + b1 * residual demand (GW) + b2 * gas (SAP, GBP/MWh, previous gas day)
--   fitted on the 60 complete days before the forecast was issued, then applied to the
--   forecast residual demand and the latest SAP.
--   estimate = 75% model + 25% the last 7 days' average price. The blend damps the model
--   when price stops tracking residual demand; it beat the model alone in every year of the
--   backtest (sql/week_ahead_backtest.sql), most on days 5-7, and 20-25% was the best weight
--   in both halves of the history.
--   Residual demand = demand minus metered (transmission) wind. Demand comes from Elexon's
--   2-14 day peak forecast (NDFD) scaled to a daily average; wind from Elexon's WINDFOR
--   (corrected) for the hours it covers, otherwise from the Open-Meteo wind forecast
--   through the lakehouse's own power curve.
--   The low/high range is +/- one standard deviation of the estimate's actual errors at
--   the same days ahead, over the issues from 67 to 8 days before this one (every one of
--   their days has a price by now), so it widens from day 1 to day 7. It held about 72% of
--   outcomes in the backtest. With fewer than 30 such errors (a fresh copy without the
--   forecast archive), it falls back to the model's own fit error, which is too narrow.
--   Gas is held at the latest SAP for the whole week.

WITH params AS (
  SELECT 60 AS fit_days, 0.25 AS last_7_days_weight, 60 AS error_issues
),

latest_issue AS (
  SELECT max(issue_date) AS issue_date FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook
),

history AS (
  SELECT
    m.date,
    m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh                       AS y,
    m.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw / 1000                    AS x1,   -- GW
    lag(m.gb_gas_sap_gbp_mwh) OVER (ORDER BY m.date)      AS x2    -- previous gas day
  FROM fact_market_daily m
  WHERE m.is_complete_day
),

-- This issue, and the past issues whose errors set the range.
issues AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.issue_date, o.issue_date = i.issue_date AS is_latest
  FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook o
  CROSS JOIN latest_issue i CROSS JOIN params p
  WHERE o.issue_date = i.issue_date
     OR (o.issue_date <  date_sub(i.issue_date, 7)
         AND o.issue_date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, 7 + p.error_issues))
),

-- Least squares with two regressors per issue, from covariances (closed form).
moments AS (
  SELECT
    s.issue_date,
    count(*) AS n,
    avg(h.y) AS my, avg(h.x1) AS m1, avg(h.x2) AS m2,
    var_pop(h.x1) AS v1, var_pop(h.x2) AS v2,
    covar_pop(h.x1, h.x2) AS c12, covar_pop(h.x1, h.y) AS c1y, covar_pop(h.x2, h.y) AS c2y
  FROM issues s
  CROSS JOIN params p
  JOIN history h
    ON h.date < s.issue_date AND h.date >= date_sub(s.issue_date, p.fit_days)
  WHERE h.y IS NOT NULL AND h.x1 IS NOT NULL AND h.x2 IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY s.issue_date
),

model AS (
  SELECT
    issue_date, n, my, m1, m2,
    (c1y * v2 - c2y * c12) / (v1 * v2 - c12 * c12) AS b1,
    (c2y * v1 - c1y * c12) / (v1 * v2 - c12 * c12) AS b2
  FROM moments
),

coefs AS (
  SELECT issue_date, n, b1, b2, my - b1 * m1 - b2 * m2 AS a FROM model
),

recent AS (
  SELECT
    s.issue_date,
    avg(m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh)   AS last_7d_price,
    avg(m.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw)/1000  AS last_7d_residual_gw
  FROM issues s
  JOIN fact_market_daily m
    ON m.date >= date_sub(s.issue_date, 7) AND m.date < s.issue_date
  GROUP BY s.issue_date
),

estimates AS (
  SELECT
    o.*,
    s.is_latest,
    c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh
                                                                            AS model_estimate,
    (1 - p.last_7_days_weight)
      * (c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh)
      + p.last_7_days_weight * r.last_7d_price                              AS estimate
  FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook o
  JOIN issues s ON s.issue_date = o.issue_date
  JOIN coefs c ON c.issue_date = o.issue_date
  JOIN recent r ON r.issue_date = o.issue_date
  CROSS JOIN params p
),

-- How far off the estimate was at each days ahead, over the past issues.
past_error AS (
  SELECT
    e.days_ahead,
    count(*)                                              AS n,
    stddev_pop(e.estimate - a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh) AS sd
  FROM estimates e
  JOIN fact_market_daily a
    ON a.date = e.target_date AND a.is_complete_day
  WHERE NOT e.is_latest AND a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY e.days_ahead
),

-- Fallback: the model's own fit error on its training days.
fit_error AS (
  SELECT stddev_pop(h.y - (c.a + c.b1 * h.x1 + c.b2 * h.x2)) AS sd
  FROM coefs c
  CROSS JOIN latest_issue i
  CROSS JOIN params p
  JOIN history h
    ON h.date < i.issue_date AND h.date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, p.fit_days)
  WHERE c.issue_date = i.issue_date
    AND h.y IS NOT NULL AND h.x1 IS NOT NULL AND h.x2 IS NOT NULL
)

SELECT
  o.target_date                                         AS day,
  date_format(o.target_date, 'EEE')                     AS weekday,
  o.days_ahead,
  round(o.demand_avg_forecast_mw / 1000, 1)             AS demand_gw,
  round(o.wind_forecast_mw / 1000, 1)                   AS wind_gw,
  o.wind_source,
  round(o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000, 1)        AS residual_demand_gw,
  round(o.avg_wind_speed_100m_ms, 1)                    AS wind_speed_ms,
  round(o.avg_temp_c, 1)                                AS temp_c,
  round(o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh, 1)                        AS gas_sap_gbp_mwh,
  round(o.latest_ttf_eur_mwh, 1)                        AS gas_ttf_eur_mwh,
  round(o.estimate, 0)                                  AS price_estimate_gbp_mwh,
  round(o.estimate - rng.sd, 0)                         AS price_low_gbp_mwh,
  round(o.estimate + rng.sd, 0)                         AS price_high_gbp_mwh,
  round(o.model_estimate, 0)                            AS model_only_estimate_gbp_mwh,
  round(r.last_7d_price, 0)                             AS last_7_days_avg_price_gbp_mwh,
  -- Model context, the same on every row
  round(c.b1, 2)                                        AS gbp_per_gw_residual,
  round(c.b2, 2)                                        AS gbp_per_gbp_gas,
  c.n                                                   AS days_in_fit,
  rng.source                                            AS range_source,
  o.issue_date,
  o.issued_utc                                          AS weather_issued_utc,
  o.demand_forecast_published_utc
FROM estimates o
JOIN coefs c ON c.issue_date = o.issue_date
JOIN recent r ON r.issue_date = o.issue_date
CROSS JOIN fit_error f
LEFT JOIN past_error pe ON pe.days_ahead = o.days_ahead
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN pe.n >= 30 THEN pe.sd ELSE f.sd END AS sd,
    CASE WHEN pe.n >= 30 THEN format_string('past errors (%d)', pe.n)
         ELSE 'model fit error (too few past errors)' END AS source
) rng
WHERE o.is_latest
ORDER BY o.target_date

datasets.name: backtest_kpis
queryLines:
-- Backtest of the week-ahead GB power price report: how far off it was, by days ahead.
--
-- Replays sql/week_ahead_report.sql for every past issue in fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook
-- (rebuilt from Open-Meteo's archive back to Mar 2024, then the live daily fetches): the
-- same model refitted on the 60 complete days before each issue, applied to that issue's
-- forecasts, blended 75/25 with the last 7 days' average price, and compared with the day's
-- market index price once it is known.
-- Replace `energy` with your catalog.
--
-- Columns, per days_ahead (1 = tomorrow):
--   mae_report            the report's estimate (model blended with the last 7 days)
--   mae_model_only        the model alone, without the blend
--   mae_last_7_days       "same as the last 7 days" (the baseline to beat)
--   mae_actual_residual   the model alone fed the residual demand that actually happened:
--                         the gap to mae_model_only is what forecasting demand and wind costs
--   bias_report           mean of estimate minus actual (positive = too high)
--   mae_residual_gw       how far off the residual demand forecast was
--   share_late_hours      share of days using a weather forecast made after the issue time
--                         (archived issues only, late on day 7: the archive keeps 7 days
--                         of lead), so day 7 is slightly flattered

WITH params AS (
  SELECT 0.25 AS last_7_days_weight                  -- as in sql/week_ahead_report.sql
),

history AS (
  SELECT
    m.date,
    m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh                       AS y,
    m.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw / 1000                    AS x1,   -- GW
    lag(m.gb_gas_sap_gbp_mwh) OVER (ORDER BY m.date)      AS x2    -- previous gas day
  FROM fact_market_daily m
  WHERE m.is_complete_day
),

issues AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT issue_date FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook
),

-- Two-regressor least squares per issue, from covariances (as in the report).
moments AS (
  SELECT
    i.issue_date,
    count(*) AS n,
    avg(h.y) AS my, avg(h.x1) AS m1, avg(h.x2) AS m2,
    var_pop(h.x1) AS v1, var_pop(h.x2) AS v2,
    covar_pop(h.x1, h.x2) AS c12, covar_pop(h.x1, h.y) AS c1y, covar_pop(h.x2, h.y) AS c2y
  FROM issues i
  JOIN history h
    ON h.date < i.issue_date AND h.date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, 60)
  WHERE h.y IS NOT NULL AND h.x1 IS NOT NULL AND h.x2 IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY i.issue_date
),

coefs AS (
  SELECT
    issue_date, n, b1, b2, my - b1 * m1 - b2 * m2 AS a
  FROM (
    SELECT
      issue_date, n, my, m1, m2,
      (c1y * v2 - c2y * c12) / (v1 * v2 - c12 * c12) AS b1,
      (c2y * v1 - c1y * c12) / (v1 * v2 - c12 * c12) AS b2
    FROM moments
  )
  WHERE n >= 30                                     -- skip issues with a thin fit window
),

recent AS (
  SELECT i.issue_date, avg(m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh) AS last_7d_price
  FROM issues i
  JOIN fact_market_daily m
    ON m.date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, 7) AND m.date < i.issue_date
  GROUP BY i.issue_date
),

scored AS (
  SELECT
    o.issue_date,
    o.days_ahead,
    o.is_archived_forecast,
    o.forecast_lead_shortfall_hours,
    a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh                                        AS actual,
    c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh
                                                                            AS model_estimate,
    (1 - p.last_7_days_weight)
      * (c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh)
      + p.last_7_days_weight * r.last_7d_price                              AS estimate,
    c.a + c.b1 * a.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh
                                                                            AS estimate_actual_residual,
    r.last_7d_price,
    (o.residual_demand_forecast_mw - a.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw) / 1000   AS residual_error_gw
  FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook o
  JOIN coefs c ON c.issue_date = o.issue_date
  JOIN recent r ON r.issue_date = o.issue_date
  CROSS JOIN params p
  JOIN fact_market_daily a
    ON a.date = o.target_date AND a.is_complete_day
  WHERE a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
    AND o.residual_demand_forecast_mw IS NOT NULL
    AND o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
)

-- needs: backtest
-- One row of headline numbers for the counters.
SELECT
  round(avg(CASE WHEN days_ahead = 1 THEN abs(estimate - actual) END), 1)       AS day1_error,
  round(avg(CASE WHEN days_ahead = 1 THEN abs(last_7d_price - actual) END), 1)  AS day1_naive_error,
  round(1 - avg(CASE WHEN days_ahead = 1 THEN abs(estimate - actual) END)
          / avg(CASE WHEN days_ahead = 1 THEN abs(last_7d_price - actual) END), 3)
                                                                                AS day1_improvement,
  round(avg(CASE WHEN days_ahead = 7 THEN abs(estimate - actual) END), 1)       AS day7_error,
  count(DISTINCT issue_date)                                                    AS issues_scored
FROM scored

coefs AS (

    SELECT

),

recent AS (
  SELECT i.issue_date, avg(m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh) AS last_7d_price
  FROM issues i
  JOIN fact_market_daily m
    ON m.date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, 7) AND m.date < i.issue_date

  SELECT
    o.issue_date,
    o.days_ahead,
    o.is_archived_forecast,
    o.forecast_lead_shortfall_hours,
    a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh                                        AS actual,
    c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh
                                                                            AS model_estimate,
    (1 - p.last_7_days_weight)
      * (c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh)
      + p.last_7_days_weight * r.last_7d_price                              AS estimate,

datasets.displayName: Day-ahead estimate against actual, last 120 days

-- Backtest of the week-ahead GB power price report: how far off it was, by days ahead.

--
-- Columns, per days_ahead (1 = tomorrow):
--   mae_report            the report's estimate (model blended with the last 7 days)
--   mae_model_only        the model alone, without the blend
--   mae_last_7_days       "same as the last 7 days" (the baseline to beat)
--   mae_actual_residual   the model alone fed the residual demand that actually happened:
--                         the gap to mae_model_only is what forecasting demand and wind costs
--   bias_report           mean of estimate minus actual (positive = too high)
--   mae_residual_gw       how far off the residual demand forecast was
--   share_late_hours      share of days using a weather forecast made after the issue time
--                         (archived issues only, late on day 7: the archive keeps 7 days
--                         of lead), so day 7 is slightly flattered

WITH params AS (
  SELECT 0.25 AS last_7_days_weight                  -- as in sql/week_ahead_report.sql
),

history AS (
  SELECT
    m.date,
    m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh                       AS y,
    m.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw / 1000                    AS x1,   -- GW
    lag(m.gb_gas_sap_gbp_mwh) OVER (ORDER BY m.date)      AS x2    -- previous gas day
  FROM fact_market_daily m
  WHERE m.is_complete_day
),

issues AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT issue_date FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook
),

-- Two-regressor least squares per issue, from covariances (as in the report).
moments AS (
  SELECT
    i.issue_date,
    count(*) AS n,
    avg(h.y) AS my, avg(h.x1) AS m1, avg(h.x2) AS m2,
    var_pop(h.x1) AS v1, var_pop(h.x2) AS v2,
    covar_pop(h.x1, h.x2) AS c12, covar_pop(h.x1, h.y) AS c1y, covar_pop(h.x2, h.y) AS c2y
  FROM issues i
  JOIN history h
    ON h.date < i.issue_date AND h.date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, 60)
  WHERE h.y IS NOT NULL AND h.x1 IS NOT NULL AND h.x2 IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY i.issue_date
),

coefs AS (
  SELECT
    issue_date, n, b1, b2, my - b1 * m1 - b2 * m2 AS a
  FROM (
    SELECT
      issue_date, n, my, m1, m2,
      (c1y * v2 - c2y * c12) / (v1 * v2 - c12 * c12) AS b1,
      (c2y * v1 - c1y * c12) / (v1 * v2 - c12 * c12) AS b2
    FROM moments
  )
  WHERE n >= 30                                     -- skip issues with a thin fit window
),

recent AS (
  SELECT i.issue_date, avg(m.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh) AS last_7d_price
  FROM issues i
  JOIN fact_market_daily m
    ON m.date >= date_sub(i.issue_date, 7) AND m.date < i.issue_date
  GROUP BY i.issue_date
),

scored AS (
  SELECT
    o.issue_date,
    o.days_ahead,
    o.is_archived_forecast,
    o.forecast_lead_shortfall_hours,
    a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh                                        AS actual,
    c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh
                                                                            AS model_estimate,
    (1 - p.last_7_days_weight)
      * (c.a + c.b1 * o.residual_demand_forecast_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh)
      + p.last_7_days_weight * r.last_7d_price                              AS estimate,
    c.a + c.b1 * a.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw / 1000 + c.b2 * o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh
                                                                            AS estimate_actual_residual,
    r.last_7d_price,
    (o.residual_demand_forecast_mw - a.gb_avg_residual_demand_mw) / 1000   AS residual_error_gw
  FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook o
  JOIN coefs c ON c.issue_date = o.issue_date
  JOIN recent r ON r.issue_date = o.issue_date
  CROSS JOIN params p
  JOIN fact_market_daily a
    ON a.date = o.target_date AND a.is_complete_day
  WHERE a.gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
    AND o.residual_demand_forecast_mw IS NOT NULL
    AND o.latest_sap_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
)

-- needs: backtest
-- The day-ahead estimate against what happened, for the last 120 days.
SELECT
  date_add(issue_date, days_ahead)   AS day,
  round(actual, 1)                   AS actual_price,
  round(estimate, 1)                 AS day_ahead_estimate
FROM scored
WHERE days_ahead = 1
  AND date_add(issue_date, days_ahead) >= date_sub(current_date(), 120)
ORDER BY day

datasets.name: market_kpis
queryLines:
-- One row of headline numbers for the counters.
WITH days AS (
  SELECT date, gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh AS price, avg_wind_share
  FROM fact_market_daily
  WHERE is_complete_day AND gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  max(date)                                                                     AS latest_day,
  round(max_by(price, date), 0)                                                 AS latest_price,
  round(avg(CASE WHEN date > date_sub(current_date(), 31) THEN price END), 0)   AS avg_price_30d,
  round(avg(CASE WHEN date > date_sub(current_date(), 396)
                  AND date <= date_sub(current_date(), 365) THEN price END), 0) AS avg_price_30d_last_year,
  round(avg(CASE WHEN date > date_sub(current_date(), 31) THEN avg_wind_share END), 3)
                                                                                AS wind_share_30d
FROM days

datasets.name: market_daily
datasets.displayName: Daily price and drivers, last two years
queryLines:
-- Complete days over the last two years: price and its two main drivers.
SELECT
  date,
  CAST(year(date) AS STRING)                    AS year,
  round(gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh, 1)       AS price,
  round(gb_avg_residual_demand_mw / 1000, 2)    AS residual_demand_gw,
  round(avg_wind_share * 100, 1)                AS wind_share_pct,
  round(gb_gas_sap_gbp_mwh, 1)                  AS gas_sap,
  round(ttf_gbp_mwh, 1)                         AS gas_ttf
FROM fact_market_daily
WHERE is_complete_day
  AND date >= add_months(current_date(), -24)
ORDER BY date

datasets.name: neighbours
datasets.displayName: GB and neighbouring markets, last 180 days
queryLines:
-- GB against its interconnected neighbours, last 180 days, one row per market and day.
SELECT date, market, round(price, 1) AS price
FROM fact_market_daily
LATERAL VIEW stack(4,
  'GB',           gb_market_index_price_gbp_mwh,
  'France',       fr_avg_price_gbp_mwh,
  'Netherlands',  nl_avg_price_gbp_mwh,
  'Norway (NO2)', no2_avg_price_gbp_mwh) AS market, price
WHERE date >= date_sub(current_date(), 180)
  AND is_complete_day
  AND price IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY date, market

datasets.name: platform_kpis
queryLines:
-- One row of headline numbers for the counters.
WITH jobs AS (
  SELECT job_id, name
  FROM system.lakeflow.jobs
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY job_id ORDER BY change_time DESC) = 1
),
daily AS (
  SELECT r.result_state
  FROM system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline r
  JOIN jobs j ON j.job_id = r.job_id
  WHERE j.name = 'energy-daily'
    AND r.result_state IS NOT NULL
    AND r.period_start_time >= date_sub(current_date(), 30)
)
SELECT
  (SELECT count(*) FROM daily WHERE result_state = 'SUCCEEDED')   AS daily_runs_ok,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM daily)                                    AS daily_runs,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM dq_settlement_period_completeness
    WHERE date >= date_sub(current_date(), 30)
      AND date < (SELECT max(settlement_date) FROM fact_gb_half_hourly))
                                                                  AS incomplete_days_30d

datasets.name: freshness
queryLines:
-- Latest day loaded per source, against how far behind each is allowed to be.
WITH latest AS (
  SELECT 'Elexon: GB prices' AS source, max(settlement_date) AS latest_day, 1 AS allowed_days_behind
  FROM fact_gb_half_hourly WHERE market_index_price_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Elexon: demand forecast', max(to_date(demand_forecast_published_utc)), 1
  FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Open-Meteo: weather forecast', max(to_date(issued_utc)), 1
  FROM fact_gb_week_ahead_outlook WHERE NOT is_archived_forecast
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'ENTSO-E: EU day-ahead prices', max(to_date(hour_utc)), 1
  FROM fact_eu_day_ahead_hourly
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'National Gas: SAP', max(date), 2
  FROM fact_market_daily WHERE gb_gas_sap_gbp_mwh IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'yfinance: TTF gas', max(date), 4
  FROM fact_market_daily WHERE ttf_eur_mwh IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'FRED: FX rates', max(date), 10
  FROM fact_market_daily WHERE usd_per_gbp IS NOT NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'yfinance: share prices', max(trade_date), 4
  FROM fact_stock_returns_daily
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 'Copernicus: ERA5 weather', max(to_date(valid_time_utc)), 14
  FROM gb_weather_hourly
)
SELECT
  source,
  latest_day,
  datediff(current_date(), latest_day)   AS days_behind,
  allowed_days_behind,
  CASE WHEN latest_day IS NULL THEN 'No data'
       WHEN datediff(current_date(), latest_day) <= allowed_days_behind THEN 'OK'
       ELSE 'Late' END                   AS status
FROM latest
ORDER BY source

datasets.name: incomplete_days
queryLines:
-- Settlement days in the last 30 with fewer half-hours loaded than the day has
-- (46, 48 or 50), before the latest day loaded (which is still filling, as is yesterday
-- until the morning run). Empty when everything is complete. Same rule as energy_checks.
SELECT date, expected_settlement_periods, periods_loaded
FROM dq_settlement_period_completeness
WHERE date >= date_sub(current_date(), 30)
  AND date < (SELECT max(settlement_date) FROM fact_gb_half_hourly)
ORDER BY date

datasets.name: job_runs
queryLines:
-- Finished runs of the prod jobs over the last 30 days, by day and outcome.
WITH jobs AS (
  SELECT job_id, name
  FROM system.lakeflow.jobs
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY job_id ORDER BY change_time DESC) = 1
)
SELECT
  to_date(r.period_start_time)   AS run_date,
  j.name                         AS job,
  r.result_state,
  count(*)                       AS runs
FROM system.lakeflow.job_run_timeline r
JOIN jobs j ON j.job_id = r.job_id
WHERE j.name IN ('energy-daily', 'energy-checks', 'energy-weekly-weather', 'energy-backfill')
  AND r.result_state IS NOT NULL
  AND r.period_start_time >= date_sub(current_date(), 30)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY run_date, job

datasets.name: cost_daily
datasets.displayName: Project cost per day, last 30 days
queryLines:
-- Databricks list-price cost of this project per day, product and environment, last 30
-- days. Jobs and the warehouse carry the project tag; the pipeline is matched by name.
-- The environment comes from the job or pipeline name: "[ci] " for the CI copy, "[dev "
-- for a developer's copy, no prefix for prod. The warehouse is shared by all of them.
-- Excludes Azure storage, and predictive optimization, which isn't attributed to a project.
WITH jobs AS (
  SELECT job_id, name
  FROM system.lakeflow.jobs
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY job_id ORDER BY change_time DESC) = 1
),
pipelines AS (
  SELECT pipeline_id, name
  FROM system.lakeflow.pipelines
  WHERE name LIKE '%energy-medallion'
  QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY pipeline_id ORDER BY change_time DESC) = 1
)
SELECT
  u.usage_date,
  CASE u.billing_origin_product
    WHEN 'DLT'  THEN 'Pipeline'
    WHEN 'JOBS' THEN 'Jobs'
    WHEN 'SQL'  THEN 'SQL warehouse'
    ELSE initcap(u.billing_origin_product) END                 AS product,
  CASE
    WHEN u.billing_origin_product = 'SQL'                THEN 'Shared (warehouse)'
    WHEN coalesce(pl.name, j.name) LIKE '[ci] %'         THEN 'CI'
    WHEN coalesce(pl.name, j.name) LIKE '[dev %'         THEN 'Dev'
    WHEN coalesce(pl.name, j.name) IS NULL               THEN 'Unknown'
    ELSE 'Prod' END                                            AS environment,
  round(sum(u.usage_quantity * p.pricing.default), 2)          AS usd
FROM system.billing.usage u
JOIN system.billing.list_prices p
  ON u.sku_name = p.sku_name
 AND u.usage_start_time >= p.price_start_time
 AND (p.price_end_time IS NULL OR u.usage_start_time < p.price_end_time)
LEFT JOIN pipelines pl ON pl.pipeline_id = u.usage_metadata.dlt_pipeline_id
LEFT JOIN jobs j ON j.job_id = u.usage_metadata.job_id
WHERE u.usage_date >= date_sub(current_date(), 30)
  AND (u.custom_tags['project'] = 'energy-markets-lakehouse' OR pl.pipeline_id IS NOT NULL)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY u.usage_date, product, environment
